To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“the radiosensitivity of E. coli cells is altered through modification of cellular DNA content.”
the radiosensitivity of cells is increased if they have previously been exposed to a mutagen.

chloramphenicol, an antibiotic which inhibits protein synthesis, enhances the survival of irradiated bacteria, while the antibiotic puromycin, which is a protein chain terminator, does not produce such an effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the DNA in the survival of cells exposed to ionizing radiation.
the role of DNA in the radiation response of E. coli.
the effect of the inhibition of protein and DNA synthesis on the radiosensitivity of E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radiosensitivity of E. coli can be modified by the prior growth of the cells in the presence of certain metabolic inhibitors.
the presence of “surplus” RNA in the cell is responsible for the increased survival of cells treated in the manner described.
the radiosensitivity of E. coli can be modified by altering the composition of the cellular macromolecular content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiosensitivity of E. coli is altered by modification of the cellular macromolecular constituents, i.e. the radiosensitivity of the cell depends upon its macromolecular content.
DNA is the primary target for X-irradiation and that the radiosensitivity of E. coli cells is determined by the amount of DNA present in the cell.
the presence in cells of a “surplus” amount of DNA, whether or not the cells are synthesizing DNA at the time of irradiation, increases the number of survivors of X-ray exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chloramphenicols can be used to increase the radiosensitivity of bacteria.
the presence or absence of thymine can be used to alter the radiosensitivity of bacteria and that the mechanism of this effect is related to the synthesis of DNA.
the DNA content is not a major factor in the radiosensitivity and that the RNA and protein contents are the most important factors.
